items.title: GitArt Rehearsal Room and Studio Website
items.cardDescription: A complex frontend app for a fictional rehearsal room and studio in Budapest, with dynamic data loading and an hourly online booking system.
items.intro: GitArt is a fictional rehearsal room and studio website that models the frontend side of a real business. The goal was to build an app that works both as an information website and as an interactive booking system with clear rules.

detailBlocks.content: The app shows the rehearsal room services, its story, the three rentable rooms, and the studio equipment. The data comes from a separate backend API, so the frontend works with real dynamic data instead of static content.

The main part of the project is the online room booking system. It is not just a simple form, but a state-based flow with several rules. Users can register, log in, and manage their own bookings in their profile.

The booking logic checks available time slots, existing bookings, and the rule that a booking can only use connected time periods. A user can book only one room at a time, and only for current or future dates.
The site also has a separate events section, so the project works as a full presentation and service website, not only as a technical demo.

detailBlocks.title: Main frontend features
items: Dynamic data display from a backend API
Detailed pages for three rehearsal rooms and one studio
JWT-based session handling on the client side
User profile and personal booking management
Booking rules for time slots and availability

detailBlocks.content: During development, an important goal was clear state handling, good control of the booking logic, and fast feedback for the user at every step.
Special attention was given to component-based structure, reusability, and the clean separation of routing and user state handling.

projectMeta.role: Frontend development, UI design, and client-side logic

items.seoDescription: The frontend of a fictional rehearsal room and studio website built with React and JavaScript, with booking logic and dynamic API data.

items.title: Electric Guitar Shop Webshop Frontend
items.cardDescription: A complex frontend app for a music webshop with product browsing, search, cart handling, authentication, and a full checkout flow.
items.intro: Electric Guitar Shop is the client-side frontend of a fictional music store and online webshop. The goal was to build a modern and responsive e-commerce interface that supports the full shopping flow through a real API connection.

detailBlocks.content: This project is a full webshop frontend that works both as a product showcase and as an interactive shopping interface. Users can browse categories, open product pages, and find products faster with search, filtering, and sorting.

The client app talks to a real backend API, so product data, user profile data, order data, and authentication all work dynamically. One important goal was to make the frontend feel like a real e-commerce system, not only a static demo.

The shopping flow goes from cart handling to checkout. The cart is saved in localStorage, so it stays after refresh, while the login state is handled with sessionStorage. During checkout, shipping data is prefilled from the user profile.
Authentication and profile handling were also important parts of the project. Registered users can log in, edit profile data, manage shipping addresses, check old orders, and change their password.

The frontend architecture is built around three Contexts. AuthContext handles login state, CartContext handles cart and checkout logic, and SearchContext shares the search text globally. This structure helps keep state handling clear and maintainable.
Client-side routing uses HashRouter, which was a conscious choice because of the GitHub Pages hosting setup. This shows that technical decisions were also shaped by the target environment.

detailBlocks.title: Main frontend features
items: Product listing by category and subcategory
Search by name, brand, category, and subcategory
Filtering by brand, color, and model
Add products to cart with custom quantity
Static info pages and contact page

detailBlocks.content: The main challenge was to make product browsing, search, filtering, cart logic, authentication, and profile handling work together as one clear user experience.

projectMeta.role: Frontend development, client-side state handling, and e-commerce flow design

items.title: MS SQL Database for the EGS Webshop
items.cardDescription: A relational database design project built with MS SQL Server for handling users, products, and orders.
items.intro: This project was made to design and build the relational database of the Electric Guitar Shop webshop in an MS SQL Server environment.

detailBlocks.content: The goal was to create a relational database that can manage the main entities and relationships of a webshop in a clear and scalable structure.
The project was created as the final work of my database specialist training. The goal was to model a real business case with a fully documented database system.

The data model handles users, products, orders, and related lookup tables. Important goals were clear structure, consistent data, and a normalized design that reduces redundancy and supports efficient queries.

detailBlocks.title: Main project parts
items: Relational data model based on an ER diagram
Structure normalized up to third normal form (3NF)
Handling users, partners, and order data

detailBlocks.content: The database stores data in several logical parts. User and partner data are kept in separate tables, while the ordering system uses a header-and-item structure. Products are linked to categories and brands, which makes the system easier to scale.
An important part is the dynamic product property system. It uses a junction-table solution, so different guitar types can have different properties without changing the database structure.

detailBlocks.title: Technical solutions
items: Primary and foreign keys for referential integrity
Check constraints and other rules for valid data
Triggers for automatic data handling processes

detailBlocks.content: The system also supports part of the business logic on the database level with tools like triggers and calculated fields, which helps keep data integrity and consistent behavior.
A key goal was to make the database not only technically correct, but also a stable and logical base for a real webshop backend.
The documentation includes the full database structure, the table descriptions, and a detailed explanation of the relationships and business logic.

items.title: Electric Guitar Shop Webshop Backend
items.cardDescription: A Node.js, Express, and MongoDB backend service for a music webshop client and admin panel, with JWT authentication and role-based access control.
items.intro: The EGS backend is the server-side app for the webshop client and admin interface. It handles products, orders, users, newsletter subscriptions, and the main business logic through a REST API.

detailBlocks.content: The goal was to build a backend layer that can reliably serve the main flows of a modern webshop. The server handles product queries, customer registration and login, profile actions, order handling, and admin endpoints.

The system is built with Express, and the data is stored in MongoDB through Mongoose models. The backend separates public endpoints, logged-in user endpoints, and admin-only endpoints, so each role has its own clear set of actions.

Authentication uses JWT tokens, and passwords are stored as hashes with bcrypt. Admin and customer access are checked through separate middleware, so the system supports both login and role-based permissions.

The backend also supports file upload for product handling, so product images are part of the server-side flow. It also serves static content, including an HTML API documentation page and product image files.

An important part of the project was that both the webshop client and the admin panel could use the same backend base. Because of this, the server supports public product data, customer actions, and admin functions at the same time.

detailBlocks.title: Main backend tasks
items: Public product list and product details
Order creation and order data handling

detailBlocks.content: During development, the main focus was a clean server structure, consistent data handling, safe authentication, and a predictable API that works well for both the client and the admin side.

projectMeta.role: API development, authentication, access control, and server-side business logic

items.title: Wordy - English-Hungarian Flashcard App
items.cardDescription: A full-stack language learning app with custom authentication, SQLite database, and a live DigitalOcean deployment.
items.intro: Wordy is a full-stack English-Hungarian flashcard app that lets users create, manage, and practice their own word packs in a modern database-based system.

detailBlocks.content: The goal was to build a web app that covers the full learning flow, from registration and word pack management to interactive practice.

The app was built with a full-stack approach using the Next.js App Router. Backend logic runs in Route Handlers, data is managed with Prisma ORM and SQLite, and authentication uses a custom session-based solution with HTTP-only cookies.
Users can create their own word packs, edit them, and practice with an interactive flashcard view. The cards are shuffled for every session, and the app also supports reverse language direction.

The live version runs on a DigitalOcean Ubuntu droplet, where the Node.js server and the SQLite database work together. The deployment uses a reverse proxy and a process manager for stable availability.
There is also a demo user account, so the main features can be tested quickly without a new registration.

Random card order for each practice session

items.title: Electric Guitar Shop Webshop Admin Panel
items.cardDescription: A React-based admin panel for managing products, orders, users, admin accounts, and newsletter subscriptions in a webshop environment.
items.intro: The EGS Admin Panel is a separate frontend app made for admin users of the Electric Guitar Shop webshop. The goal was to build a clear and usable admin interface on top of the same backend as the client webshop.

detailBlocks.content: The admin interface is a standalone React app that supports the most important background tasks of the webshop. After login, admins can use a central dashboard to reach products, orders, users, admin accounts, and newsletter actions.

The system uses token-based admin authentication. After a successful login, protected routes and actions are available only for authenticated admins. The auth state is handled by Context API, and the token is stored in sessionStorage.

The dashboard loads data from several endpoints and shows summary numbers like customer count, order count, product count, and total revenue. This makes the app useful not only as an admin tool, but also as a simple monitoring view.

The product module supports list, detail, create, and edit views, with category filtering and pagination. Filter state is also saved in localStorage, so the admin workflow can continue more comfortably after refresh.

The order management screen supports listing, detailed viewing, editing, and deleting orders. Customers and admins are shown in two separate views based on the same user data source and the IsAdmin field.
The project also includes personal admin profile handling and newsletter subscription management. Profile updates use client-side validation, and phone numbers are checked with libphonenumber-js.

items: Admin login and token-based access control
Dashboard with summary numbers and short statistics
List, filter, paginate, create, edit, and delete products
List, view, edit, and delete orders
Create, edit, and delete admin accounts
Responsive admin interface with collapsible sidebar

detailBlocks.content: During development, it was important to organize the more complex admin tasks into a clear interface and to make the CRUD flows feel consistent across different entities.

items.title: GitArt Rehearsal Room and Studio Backend
items.cardDescription: A backend app for a rehearsal room booking system, with JWT authentication, MongoDB data handling, email notifications, and documented API endpoints.
items.intro: The GitArt backend is the server-side part of the rehearsal room and studio web app. It supports user handling, booking logic, room and studio data, and email notifications.

detailBlocks.content: The goal was to build a backend system that can support the main business flows of a real rehearsal room website. The server handles registration, login, authentication, profile data, and the creation, listing, and deletion of bookings.

The backend is built with Express, and data is stored in MongoDB through Mongoose models. It provides separate endpoints for rooms, studio data, and bookings, so the frontend can load everything dynamically through the API.

User identification is based on JWT. Public and protected endpoints are separated with middleware, so the system can handle actions that are available only for logged-in users, such as profile and personal booking queries.

One interesting part of the project is the email logic. Booking confirmation and reminder emails are not handled only in Node.js, because the server also calls a Python SMTP script in the background. Timed reminders are handled with node-schedule.

The backend also includes a visual API documentation page where endpoints can be reviewed and tested, and each request has copyable fetch examples. This is useful for frontend integration and developer testing.
The project runs on an Ubuntu-based DigitalOcean droplet, so the server-side behavior can be tested not only locally but also in a real hosted environment.

detailBlocks.title: Main backend tasks
items: Create new bookings and delete old ones
Serve room and studio data through the API
MongoDB data handling with Mongoose models
Email sending through a Python SMTP script
Visual API documentation with copyable fetch examples

detailBlocks.content: The main challenge was to make authentication, booking logic, timed email flows, and a modular server structure work together well. A lot of attention was given to the separation of routes, controllers, models, middleware, and helper functions.

items.title: MongoDB Database for the Electric Guitar Shop Webshop
items.cardDescription: A MongoDB database for webshop use, handling users, products, orders, and newsletter subscriptions.
items.intro: This project is the MongoDB-based database of the Electric Guitar Shop webshop. The data model supports the client side and the admin panel, and it handles users, products, orders, and newsletter subscriptions.

detailBlocks.content: The goal was to create a NoSQL database that fits a real webshop backend and can handle different data shapes in a flexible way. In practice, the MongoDB approach was easier to use for hosting and real operation than the separate MS SQL version. The database runs on an Ubuntu-based DigitalOcean server together with the webshop backend.
The database is built around four main collections: users, products, orders, and newsletter. Together they cover the main data needed for the webshop.

The users collection stores both customer and admin data. The documents include user ID, username, hashed password, admin flags, personal data, contact data, and fields for shipping and billing addresses.

The products collection stores the webshop catalog. Each document includes product ID, name, category, subcategory, brand, technical and visual details, price, description, and image path. The document model works well here because different product types can have different fields.

The orders collection stores order header data and embedded order items in one document. This includes order ID, customer ID, status, date, shipping data, totals, and an OrderItems array. This structure fits the reading and admin needs of the order flow well.
The newsletter collection is simpler. It stores email addresses and active status for newsletter subscriptions, which keeps marketing data separate from user accounts.

detailBlocks.title: Main collection roles
items: users - customer and admin data, permissions, and addresses
products - product data, technical details, price, and image path
orders - order header data and embedded order items
newsletter - subscriber email addresses and active status

detailBlocks.title: Important model features
items: Hashed passwords in the users collection
Customer and admin roles in one user model
Embedded order items inside order documents
A model that fits both the client and admin panel

detailBlocks.content: An important design goal was that the database should support the REST API well and stay easy to use for the backend logic. Embedded order items reduce query complexity, while separate collections work well for product and user list/detail views.
This project shows how the main business flows of a webshop can be supported with a NoSQL model while keeping the system flexible, scalable, and easy to handle for the backend API.

projectMeta.role: NoSQL data model design for webshop logic

items.title: MongoDB Database for the GitArt Rehearsal Room and Studio
items.cardDescription: A document-based database for the GitArt system, handling users, rehearsal rooms, studio data, and hourly bookings.
items.intro: This project is the MongoDB-based database of the GitArt rehearsal room and studio system. The model was made to support presentation content, user activity, and the online booking flow.

detailBlocks.content: The goal was to build a document-based structure that supports both a rehearsal room website and an online booking system. The model handles presentation content, user data, and dynamic booking information at the same time.
The system uses four main collections: bookings, rooms, studio, and users. Together they cover the full data range needed for booking logic, room and studio display, and user activity.

The bookings collection stores booking data. One document includes the user ID, booking date, selected room, list of hours, booking name, and band name. This structure fits an hourly booking system well.

The rooms collection stores room data. It includes not only basic information like room name, size, and hourly price, but also detailed equipment in embedded objects. This allows the frontend to load rich room data from a single query.

The studio collection stores more complex studio data, including the basic information, detailed technical equipment, and available instruments. Because this data is hierarchical, the document model of MongoDB fits it very well.

The users collection handles user data. The documents include user ID, hashed password, booking name, personal data, email, phone number, and acceptance of the privacy rules. Passwords are stored as secure hashes.

detailBlocks.title: Main collection roles
items: bookings - bookings with date, room, and time slots
rooms - room basics and detailed equipment
studio - studio data, technical tools, and instruments
users - user data, booking name, and login information

detailBlocks.title: Important model features
items: Embedded objects for complex equipment data
Bookings linked to users by UserID
Hierarchical room and studio data in documents
Easy extension with new tools, rooms, or fields

detailBlocks.content: An important design goal was that the database should work well for both frontend display needs and backend booking logic. The document-based approach helped serve related data with fewer complex joins.
This project shows how a real business flow, in this case an online rehearsal room booking system, can be supported with a NoSQL model while keeping content and transaction data clear and extendable.

projectMeta.role: NoSQL data model design and document structure planning for a booking system

items.seoDescription: A MongoDB database of the GitArt rehearsal room and studio system, designed for users, rooms, studio data, and booking logic.

items.title: Taste It! Desktop App
items.cardDescription: A full-stack Windows desktop app based on the Taste It! recipe website, rebuilt for private local use with local data storage and desktop login.
items.intro: Taste It! Desktop App is the private Windows desktop version of my recipe website. The goal of the project was to turn the public web app into a personal recipe manager that runs locally and stores recipes, images, and user data on the computer.

detailBlocks.content: This project started from the older web version, but it was changed for desktop use. The React interface runs inside Electron, so the app feels more like a real desktop program and does not need public hosting.

The app lets users create, edit, and delete recipes, manage local recipe images, browse by category and subcategory, search recipes, save favorites, and use a profile page. It also has admin-based user management and backup export and import.

One important change in the architecture is that the old Next.js /app/api routes were removed. The React UI now talks to the backend logic through the Electron preload layer and IPC, then the services use Prisma ORM with a SQLite database.

detailBlocks.title: Main features
items: Save, replace, and delete recipe images
Remember the last logged-in user in the desktop session

detailBlocks.content: The stack uses Next.js 15.5, React 19, Electron 41, Prisma ORM 6.16.2, SQLite, and Sass modules. In the installed Windows app, Prisma uses the library engine because it is more stable in this desktop setup.

The desktop version is useful because it does not need a separate server, the database and recipe images stay local, authentication can stay simpler, and the whole app gives a more personal desktop experience.

projectMeta.role: Full-stack desktop development, Electron IPC architecture, and local data handling

about.mainTitle: Let me introduce myself in a few lines.
about.firstParagraph: My name is Thomas Horváth, originally a musician, composer, creator. I started to deal more seriously with web development in 2022.
about.secundParagraph: I like creating, learning is my hobby. I like logical systems. To solve tasks precisely, striving for perfection, but also creatively.
about.thirdParagraph: In the spring of 2022, I was given the opportunity to gain insight into the world of IT as part of the "Redesign" program. During the system operator training, I mastered computer technology principles, the basics of network operation, and the construction, use, and operation of client (Windows, Linux) and server-side (Windows Server, Linux Server) operating systems, virtual machines (Hyper-V, Docker), and cloud platforms (Azure, AWS).
about.forthParagraph: After that, I took part in database specialist training, where I learned the SQL language at an advanced level, as well as the use, configuration, and operation of various database software (MS SQL, MySQL, MongoDB). In addition, I also mastered the design and optimization of databases.
about.fifthParagraph: Due to my commitment to continuous learning, and because I always like to see the big picture, I set my sights on a full-stack development career. In addition to mastering front-end development at an advanced level, my current goal is to learn about the back-end side, with which I will be able to implement complete systems on the web development platform.

about.skillsDescription: I work with tools that allow me to build complete web solutions, from visual interfaces to server-side logic and databases.

aboutInfo.title: A Few More Things About Me
aboutInfo.firstInfoContent:
Music has been an integral part of my life since childhood. I have been playing the guitar since I was thirteen, and it remains a lifelong passion.

I graduated from the Kőbánya Music Studio as a professional guitarist. It was an immense honor to play alongside renowned Hungarian music icons such as Egon Póka, Gyula Babos, and István Vörös.

On the following page, you can learn more about my musical career: theguitarist.thomashorvath.hu
aboutInfo.secundInfoContent:
The world of computers fascinated me from a young age, during the era of MS-DOS and the Commodore 64.

Although I initially pursued music, the advent of COVID-19 radically transformed my life. Music took a backseat, but seizing a great opportunity, I began studying IT. This field ignited the same enthusiasm in me as when I first started with music.
aboutInfo.thirdInfoContent:
In my free time, I enjoy creating things. I like DIY projects and solving problems around the house, whether it's painting, electrical work, or car repairs.

I'm eager to immerse myself in learning new things. I enjoy hiking, reading, listening to music, playing guitar, and continually learning.
aboutInfo.forthInfoContent:
Fitness and bodybuilding have always amazed me. As a teenager, I eagerly went to the gym, though as I entered the professional world, I found it harder to make time for regular workouts. I plan to start exercising again soon.

My greatest inspiration is Arnold Schwarzenegger.
aboutInfo.fifthInfoContent:
You can count on me to perform my tasks reliably and precisely in any situation.

I am determined to achieve my goals while adapting easily to new situations and working effectively with others.

wrapper_content.title: 1. Data Protection and Security
wrapper_content.content: We treat your customer data as strictly confidential and take all necessary measures to protect it. Only those employees who are explicitly authorized and need access to the data for their work can access it. We conduct regular data security audits to prevent unauthorized access and security incidents.

wrapper_content.title: 2. Data Collection and Use
wrapper_content.content: We collect and use customer data solely for fair and lawful purposes. The data is used exclusively to maintain relationships with customers and to improve and enhance our services. We do not sell or disclose customer data to third parties without permission.

wrapper_content.title: 3. User Rights
wrapper_content.content: Our customers have the right to access their personal data provided to us and may request its correction or deletion if necessary. If our customers wish to express their preferences regarding data management, please contact us using the details below.

wrapper_content.title: 4. Privacy Notice and Review
wrapper_content.content: We regularly update our privacy policy to comply with legal requirements and meet customer expectations. We notify our customers of any changes, and all new data protection measures are reviewed and approved in advance.

introduction.text: When you access my portfolio website, the site may automatically save information from your computer or the device used for browsing (tablet, smartphone). For this purpose, so-called computer 'cookies' are used.

whatIsCookie.title: What is a cookie?
whatIsCookie.text: A cookie is a small piece of text that the visited website sends to your browser. It allows the site to remember information about your visit, such as the language you used and other settings. This makes your next visit smoother and easier to use. Cookies play an important role; without them, using the internet would be much more cumbersome.

cookiesPurpose.title: What types of cookies do we use and for what purpose?

types.text: Our website uses so-called 'temporary cookies' (session cookies) and 'permanent cookies'. Temporary cookies remain on your computer until you leave the website, while permanent cookies stay on your device for a longer period (depending on your browser settings), or until you manually delete them.

These are temporary cookies that are only stored for the duration of your visit. They are automatically deleted from your computer at the end of your session or when you close your browser. Session cookies are essential for navigating our website and ensuring its proper functionality. They do not collect any information that could identify you personally.

We use Google Analytics cookies to gather information about the behavior and characteristics of our visitors. This helps us make our website clearer and easier to use. These cookies do not personally identify you, for instance, we do not store your name or email address; data is collected and stored anonymously and in aggregate. Even the IP address is only partially recorded.

These cookies allow us to remember your choices on our website (e.g., the data entered on forms, etc.). These cookies track your activity solely on the visited website and not on others. They may store personal data you have provided, such as your email address.

We may use external web services on our website provided by third parties. In such cases, the storage of cookies is not controlled by us, and we have no influence over what information these external providers collect.

consentWithdrawal.title: How to withdraw consent?
consentWithdrawal.text: Consent validity may expire occasionally. However, if you wish to withdraw your consent, you can do so at any time through your browser's cookie settings.

browserSettings.title: Browser Settings
browserSettings.text: These cookies do not store personal data, such as your name, address, or payment information. If you still wish to disable, block, or delete cookies from my site, you can do so using your browser. You can find the cookie settings for major browsers here:
